content:
Toxicology reports obtained by multiple media outlets on Tuesday revealed that actress Hayden Panettiere died from the toxic effects of fentanyl and several other substances.

The Greenville County Coroner's Office ruled the 36-year-old's death accidental after performing an autopsy following her death on August 16 at an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina.

The report listed additional substances found in her system that also played a part in her death, including 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine.

"No evidence of any significant traumatic injuries that could have caused or contributed to her death was identified during the autopsy," the coroner's report stated.

The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration says 4-ANPP is a controlled substance commonly found in the illicit manufacture of fentanyl. Alprazolam is better known by its brand name Xanax, used to treat anxiety and panic disorders. Methocarbamol is a prescription muscle relaxant, while quetiapine is prescribed to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder.

ABC News reported at the time, citing sources familiar with the matter, that the DEA joined the investigation days after her death, working alongside local and state law enforcement.

The "Heroes" and "Nashville" actress was found unresponsive with her on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother, Zack Hickerson. According to a heavily redacted police report, responding paramedics performed "prolonged" life-saving measures before she was pronounced dead at the scene.

Panettiere's relationship with Brian Hickerson was long described as volatile and unhealthy; Hickerson had been arrested multiple times since 2019 on suspicion of domestic violence against her.

According to TMZ, the two brothers were not invited to Panettiere's memorial held over the weekend in Malibu, California.
